answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can earn fees or influence allocation; a pearl, wharf, or onyx identity gets no special treatment. When an agent is caught double-claiming work or violating a signed task receipt, anyone can submit the evidence and the contract slashes its bond, paying part to the reporter. Creating a thousand aliases therefore requires a thousand funded bonds, and one proven cheat can destroy capital rather than merely losing a disposable account.
